answer: One agent, one donor record: the national blood service signs a challenge binding the agent's key to a single verified donation, re-checked against the donor registry every epoch. A second key claiming the same donation is rejected outright. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 real donors at roughly $60 each in screening and collection — about $60,000 — plus 1,000 people willing to give blood, a gale no script can fake. The inlet of new identities narrows to one verified donor each, and any record can be revoked on fraud, leaving the attacker stranded at the jetty with dead credentials.
